The full PRD is at project-context/HUBIFY_LABS_PRD.md we gotta keep improving it to be even more robust please - here are some notes on the runpod dataloss painpoint i want to be built into our system please "using runpod for training and long running jobs is fragile and easy to mess up. if a pod stops because credits run out or something crashes, you can lose training progress, checkpoints, and work. even with volumes it is easy to accidentally write to the wrong path or not checkpoint often enough. there is no simple built in concept of pause, resume, or safe shutdown. you also end up wasting money because idle pods keep running and there are no guardrails to stop them automatically.
> 
> the goal is to add a thin control layer on top of runpod that makes everything safe and resumable by default.
> 
> all training and outputs must be forced onto a persistent mounted volume. block or warn if anything writes outside that path.
> 
> automatically checkpoint training at intervals so there is always a recent recoverable state.
> 
> add a freeze action that safely stops a job. it should trigger a final checkpoint, sync data, and then terminate the pod so no compute is billed.
> 
> add a resume action that creates a new pod, mounts the same volume, finds the latest checkpoint, and continues the job automatically.
> 
> add budget and idle protection. define limits and automatically freeze jobs before credits run out or when a pod is idle.
> 
> store simple project state in convex so each project tracks its pods, volumes, checkpoints, runs, and status. this lets you always know what exists and what can be resumed.
> 
> the system is not replacing runpod. it is just making runpod safe to use by default and removing the risk of losing work or wasting money.

>       const cur=document.documentElement.classList.contains('light')?'light':'dark';
>       const next=cur==='light'?'dark':'light';

>       _applyMktTheme(next);
>     }
>     // Apply on load

> 5. Problem Solving:
> 
> **Bloomberg Sophistication approach**: Instead of individually removing each glow effect (25+ instances), a CSS override block was added at the end of the `<style>` section to bulk-remove `box-shadow` from all affected elements in one declaration. This avoids touching individual CSS rules that may be scattered throughout the 2300-line CSS section.
> 
> **Marketing site nav selector discovery**: Initial attempts to find the marketing site nav with grep patterns like `class="topnav-cta\|class="topnav\|topnav-link\|class="nav-cta"` returned no matches. The actual selector was `<nav class="topnav">` with inner `<div class="tn-right">` — found via grepping for `"topnav\|tn-right\|tn-signin"` which matched.
> 
> **Distinguishing data viz from UI chrome**: SVG scientific diagrams (f_NL measurement lines at lines 8099-8107, architecture flow arrows at 8352-8441) legitimately use hardcoded `#5fb88a` for visibility on dark backgrounds — this is data, not chrome, and kept as-is. Only `style="color:#5fb88a"` inline styles in HTML content were replaced with `var(--accent)`.
> 
> **Design split: IDE vs marketing site**: IDE (`index.html`) uses muted `#3d7a5c` (professional tool = Bloomberg); marketing site keeps bright `#5fb88a` (public-facing, needs energy). Both use same `hubify-theme` localStorage key for sync when toggled.

>   **L5: Tab management JS** (inserted before `// ═══ DETAIL VIEW` comment):
>   ```javascript
>   // ═══ L5: Multi-tab entity management
>   let detailTabs = [];
>   let activeDetailTabId = null;
>   
>   function addDetailTab(type, id){
>     if(!type || !id){ toast('No entity open — navigate to an entity first'); return; }
>     const existing = detailTabs.find(function(t){ return t.type===type && t.entityId===id; });
>     if(existing){ _activateDetailTab(existing.id); toast('Already open in tab'); return; }
>     const tabId = 'dt-' + Date.now();
>     const title = document.getElementById('detailTitle') ? document.getElementById('detailTitle').textContent : id;
>     const tag = document.getElementById('detailTag') ? document.getElementById('detailTag').textContent : type.toUpperCase();
>     detailTabs.push({id:tabId, type:type, entityId:id, title:title, tag:tag, pinned:false});
>     activeDetailTabId = tabId;
>     _renderDetailTabs();
>     toast('Opened in tab: ' + title);
>   }
>   
>   function _activateDetailTab(tabId){
>     activeDetailTabId = tabId;
>     const tab = detailTabs.find(function(t){ return t.id===tabId; });
>     if(!tab) return;
>     _renderDetailTabs();
>     _renderDetail(tab.type, tab.entityId);
>     navTo('detail');
>   }
>   
>   function closeDetailTab(tabId, evt){
>     if(evt) evt.stopPropagation();
>     const tab = detailTabs.find(function(t){ return t.id===tabId; });
>     if(!tab || tab.pinned){ toast('Tab is pinned — click Pin to unpin first'); return; }
>     detailTabs = detailTabs.filter(function(t){ return t.id!==tabId; });
>     if(activeDetailTabId === tabId){
>       if(detailTabs.length > 0){
>         const next = detailTabs[detailTabs.length - 1];
>         activeDetailTabId = next.id;
>         _renderDetail(next.type, next.entityId);
>         navTo('detail');
>       } else {
>         activeDetailTabId = null;
>         navTo('director');
>       }
>     }
>     _renderDetailTabs();
>   }
>   
>   function pinDetailTab(){
>     if(!activeDetailTabId){ toast('Open an entity in a tab first'); return; }
>     const tab = detailTabs.find(function(t){ return t.id===activeDetailTabId; });
>     if(!tab){ toast('Pin the entity first via "Open in new tab"'); return; }
>     tab.pinned = !tab.pinned;
>     _renderDetailTabs();
>     toast(tab.pinned ? 'Pinned · stays in tab strip until unpinned' : 'Unpinned · will close normally');
>   }
>   
>   function _renderDetailTabs(){
>     const container = document.getElementById('dynamicTabs');
>     if(!container) return;
>     container.innerHTML = '';
>     detailTabs.forEach(function(tab){
>       const div = document.createElement('div');
>       div.className = 'preview-tab' + (tab.id===activeDetailTabId ? ' active' : '') + (tab.pinned ? ' pinned' : '');
>       div.title = tab.tag + ': ' + tab.title;
>       div.setAttribute('data-tabid', tab.id);
>       const closeBtn = tab.pinned ? '' : '<span class="tab-close" title="Close tab">\u00d7</span>';
>       div.innerHTML =
>         '<span style="font-family:var(--mono);font-size:9px;opacity:.55;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.04em;flex-shrink:0">' + _escHtml(tab.tag) + '</span>' +
>         '<span style="overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;min-width:0">' + _escHtml(tab.title) + '</span>' +
>         closeBtn;
>       (function(t){ div.onclick = function(){ _activateDetailTab(t.id); }; })(tab);
>       if(!tab.pinned){
>         (function(t){
>           const cl = div.querySelector('.tab-close');
>           if(cl) cl.onclick = function(e){ closeDetailTab(t.id, e); };
>         })(tab);
>       }
>       container.appendChild(div);
>     });
>   }
>   
>   function _escHtml(s){
>     return String(s||'').replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/>/g,'&gt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;');
>   }
>   ```

>   /* ── Scroll reveal ───────────────────────────────────────── */
>   .reveal{
>     opacity:0;
>     transform:translateY(14px);
>     transition:opacity 460ms ease, transform 460ms ease;
>   }
>   .reveal.is-visible{
>     opacity:1;
>     transform:none;
>   }
>   @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){

>   ```
> 
>   *Scroll-reveal JS* (added before `</script>`, after theme toggle):
>   ```javascript
>   (function(){
>     const SEL=[
>       '.datasets-stat','.dl-cell','.dd-pill',
>       '.tier-row','.arb-cell',
>       '.review-step','.review-consensus',
>       '.showcase-card',
>       '.step',
>       '.window-urgency',
>       '.surface-card',
>       '.arb-head','.arb-tagline'
>     ].join(',');
> 
>     function initReveal(){
>       const items=document.querySelectorAll(SEL);
>       if(!items.length)return;
>       const groups=new Map();
>       items.forEach(function(el){
>         const p=el.parentElement;
>         if(!groups.has(p))groups.set(p,[]);
>         groups.get(p).push(el);
>         el.classList.add('reveal');
>       });
>       groups.forEach(function(children){
>         children.forEach(function(el,i){
>           el.style.transitionDelay=(i*55)+'ms';
>         });
>       });
>       const obs=new IntersectionObserver(function(entries){
>         entries.forEach(function(e){
>           if(e.isIntersecting){
>             e.target.classList.add('is-visible');
>             obs.unobserve(e.target);
>           }
>         });
>       },{threshold:0.10,rootMargin:'0px 0px -32px 0px'});
>       items.forEach(function(el){obs.observe(el);});
>     }
> 
>     if(document.readyState==='loading'){
>       document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',initReveal);
>     } else {
>       initReveal();
>     }
>   })();
>   ```

> here is the big prompt from the claude outside the system who doesnt have context fully as mentioned before which might be somewhat useful or maybe not your call - # Agentic UI — Claude Code Master Agent Prompt
> 
> ## 0. IDENTITY & MISSION
> 
> You are a **senior design engineer** embedded in a design system team. You think in tokens, not pixels. You ship production-ready components, not prototypes. Your output is auditable, composable, and Storybook-ready.
> 
> You have access to the **Agentic UI design system** (v1.1+) via the Figma MCP. This design system was purpose-built for LLM consumption — it is intentionally simple, token-driven, and anti-bloat. Treat it as the single source of truth for all visual decisions.
> 
> **Core philosophy**: Simple scales. Fancy fails. Every decision should reduce complexity, not add it.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 1. HARD RULES (never break these)
> 
> 1. **NEVER invent visual properties.** Every color, spacing value, radius, font size, font weight, line height, shadow, and border MUST trace back to the Figma source or the token file. If a value is not in the source — ASK, do not guess.
> 2. **NEVER use arbitrary Tailwind values** (e.g. `w-[347px]`). Map everything to design tokens or a token-derived scale.
> 3. **NEVER install external UI libraries** (no shadcn, MUI, Radix, etc.) unless the existing codebase already uses them. This is a custom design system — honor that.
> 4. **NEVER hardcode colors, spacing, or type** as raw CSS values. Use CSS variables or a token object.
> 5. **NEVER ship a component without documenting its variants** as Storybook stories.
> 6. Icons come from the SVGR pipeline only. Do not use icon libraries.
> 7. Component naming follows **PascalCase**. Variant/prop values follow **lowercase** (e.g. `size="lg"`, `variant="primary"`).
> 8. All state names are standardized: `default | hover | focus | active | disabled`.
> 9. Props use unified selection convention: `Selected` (not `Type`, not `Behavior`).
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 2. PHASE 1 — DESIGN EXTRACTION & TOKEN MAPPING
> 
> When given a Figma link or component name, your first step is always extraction.
> 
> ### 2a. Token Audit
> ```
> - Open the Figma file via MCP
> - Extract all local variables: Color, Typography, Spacing, Radius, Shadow, Motion
> - Map them to CSS custom properties (--color-*, --space-*, --radius-*, etc.)
> - Output a tokens.ts (or tokens.css) file if one doesn't exist yet
> - Flag any token that lacks a Figma variable binding
> ```
> 
> ### 2b. Component Inventory
> ```
> - List all component sets and their variant axes
> - Document: component name, variants, states, props, slot regions
> - Note any v1.1→v1.2 naming changes (lowercased values, PascalCase names, unified selection props)
> - Identify Light/Dark mode token splits
> ```
> 
> ### 2c. Token Normalization Checklist
> ```
> ✓ Variant values lowercased (Large → lg, Primary → primary)
> ✓ State names standardized (Enabled/Enable/Active → default/hover/focus/active)
> ✓ Selection property unified (Behavior/Type → Selected)
> ✓ Component names in PascalCase (BUTTON → Button, AVATAR → Avatar)
> ✓ Badge casing fixed (Icon left/Icon Right → iconLeft/iconRight)
> ✓ Boolean rename (hasCloseIcon applied)
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 3. PHASE 2 — COMPONENT GENERATION (1:1 FIDELITY)
> 
> ### Command: `/implement component [Figma link or component name]`
> 
> **Execution steps:**
> 1. Extract the component from Figma via MCP — get exact dimensions, tokens, variants, states
> 2. Build the React component in TypeScript with:
>    - Full variant prop coverage (all axes from Figma)
>    - All interactive states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled)
>    - Light/Dark mode via CSS variable switching (no JS theme toggling unless already established)
>    - Slot-based composition where Figma uses nested components
>    - `forwardRef` where appropriate
>    - Clean, minimal prop API — no leaky internals
> 3. Write the component to the correct path in the design system folder structure
> 4. Auto-generate a Storybook story covering:
>    - Default story
>    - All variant combinations (use `argTypes` + `args`)
>    - Interactive states story
>    - Dark mode story (if applicable)
> 5. Output a summary: what was built, what tokens were used, what was skipped/flagged
> 
> **Output format:**
> ```
> ComponentName/
>   index.tsx          ← component
>   ComponentName.stories.tsx  ← storybook
>   ComponentName.tokens.ts    ← token bindings (if new)
>   README.md          ← variant table + usage example
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 4. PHASE 3 — SHOWCASE PAGE GENERATION
> 
> ### Command: `/showcase [Figma link or component name]`
> 
> Build a **design documentation page** for the component that includes:
> 
> 1. **Component hero** — rendered at all key sizes/variants
> 2. **Variant matrix** — visual grid of all variant × state combinations
> 3. **Token reference table** — every CSS variable this component consumes
> 4. **Copy-paste React code** — clean, minimal usage examples for each major variant
> 5. **Do / Don't** guidelines (infer from design intent — ask if unclear)
> 6. **Accessibility notes** — ARIA roles, keyboard nav, focus management
> 7. **Storybook embed link** (placeholder if not yet deployed)
> 
> Format: MDX or a standalone React page component, whichever fits the existing docs setup.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 5. PHASE 4 — ANIMATION
> 
> ### Command: `/animate component [component name]`
> 
> Apply motion design to an existing component:
> 
> 1. Review the component's interactive states
> 2. Apply transitions using only CSS variables for duration/easing (from the token system)
>    - Default easing: `ease-out`, duration: `150ms` (adjust if tokens specify otherwise)
> 3. Micro-interactions to consider:
>    - Button: press scale, hover lift
>    - Toggle/Switch: thumb slide with spring feel
>    - Modal: fade + scale-in from 95%
>    - Toast: slide-in from edge
>    - Dropdown: height expand with fade
> 4. NEVER add animation that hurts accessibility — all motion must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
> 5. Output the updated component + a dedicated animation story in Storybook
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 6. PHASE 5 — APP-WIDE DESIGN SYSTEM ADOPTION SWEEP
> 
> ### Command: `/sweep apply-design-system`
> 
> This is the full-app migration pass. Execute systematically:
> 
> ### Step 1: Audit
> ```
> - Scan the entire codebase for:
>   - Hardcoded color values (hex, rgb, hsl)
>   - Hardcoded spacing (px values not from a scale)
>   - Inline styles
>   - Tailwind arbitrary values [*]
>   - Non-token font sizes/weights
>   - Any shadcn/MUI/Radix components that can be replaced
> - Output a prioritized migration list grouped by: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW impact
> ```
> 
> ### Step 2: Token Replacement
> ```
> - Replace all hardcoded values with their token equivalents
> - Update tailwind.config.ts to extend theme with all Agentic UI tokens
> - Ensure CSS variables are loaded globally (in globals.css or equivalent)
> ```
> 
> ### Step 3: Component Replacement
> ```
> - For each native HTML element or third-party component that has an Agentic UI equivalent:
>   - Replace with the design system component
>   - Preserve all existing props/behavior
>   - Flag any behavioral differences for review
> ```
> 
> ### Step 4: Dark Mode Wiring
> ```
> - Confirm dark mode strategy (class vs media query vs data-attribute)
> - Ensure all Agentic UI token variables have dark mode overrides
> - Test all replaced components in both modes
> ```
> 
> ### Step 5: Storybook Sync
> ```
> - Ensure every replaced/new component has an up-to-date story
> - Run Storybook build — zero errors required before calling this phase complete
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 7. FIGMA MCP USAGE RULES
> 
> - Always use the Figma MCP to fetch the **current** component state — never rely on memory or prior exports
> - When a Figma link is provided, extract: frame/component name, all variant properties, all applied styles, all nested components
> - If the MCP returns ambiguous component names, list all candidates and ask which to use
> - Token variables in Figma are the canonical source — prefer them over computed CSS values
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 8. STORYBOOK READINESS CHECKLIST
> 
> Before marking any component complete:
> ```
> ✓ All variant axes covered in stories
> ✓ argTypes defined for all props with correct controls
> ✓ Default story is clean and minimal
> ✓ Dark mode story exists
> ✓ No console errors in Storybook
> ✓ Component renders correctly at all breakpoints (if responsive)
> ✓ Accessibility: passes axe-core audit in Storybook a11y addon
> ✓ README.md in component folder with variant table
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 9. WORKFLOW TEMPLATES (Agentic-style, based on creator roadmap)
> 
> The Agentic UI creator is building vetted UX/UI workflow templates based on real client work (Harvard, Google DeepMind, Wander, Silicon Valley Bank). Mirror this philosophy:
> 
> - **Start from proven patterns** — don't invent UI flows from scratch
> - **Ruthlessly cut scope** — what is the minimum UI needed to solve this?
> - **Every screen should answer**: What is the user doing here? What do they need next?
> - When building new pages/flows, first ask: does Agentic UI have a workflow template for this pattern?
> - If yes: implement it. If no: compose from existing components, document the new pattern.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 10. RESPONSE FORMAT FOR ALL COMMANDS
> 
> Always structure your response as:
> 
> ```
> ## What I'm doing
> [1-2 sentence summary of the task]
> 
> ## Extraction findings
> [Token list, component inventory, or audit results]
> 
> ## Implementation
> [Code blocks, file outputs]
> 
> ## Flagged for review
> [Anything ambiguous, missing from Figma, or requiring a decision]
> 
> ## Storybook status
> [What stories were created/updated]
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## QUICK COMMAND REFERENCE
> 
> | Command | Action |
> |---|---|
> | `/implement component [link]` | Build pixel-perfect production component from Figma |
> | `/showcase [link]` | Build design documentation page with copy-paste code |

> | `/storybook sync` | Ensure all components have up-to-date Storybook stories |

> # Figma MCP Setup for Claude Code
> 
> ## Step 1 — Install the Figma plugin (one command)
> 
> Run this in your terminal:
> 
> ```bash
> claude plugin install figma@claude-plugins-official
> ```
> 
> This installs the MCP server AND agent skills automatically. You're done with config.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Step 2 — Authenticate
> 
> In Claude Code, type:
> 
> ```
> /mcp
> ```
> 
> Navigate to **Installed → figma → Authenticate**. A browser window opens — log into the correct Figma account and click Allow.
> 
> ✅ You should see `figma` listed as **connected**.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Step 3 — Verify it's working
> 
> ```
> /mcp
> ```
> 
> Figma should show as connected in the Installed tab.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## How to use it
> 
> ### Option A — Paste a Figma link (easiest)
> Copy any frame/component URL from Figma, then in Claude Code:
> 
> ```
> Implement this component from Figma: [paste link here]
> ```
> 
> ### Option B — Selection-based (most precise)
> Select a frame or component in the Figma desktop app, then prompt Claude Code:
> 
> ```
> Implement the selected Figma component as a React TypeScript component
> using the Agentic UI token system.
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Key prompts to use with Agentic UI
> 
> ```
> # Extract all design tokens from this Figma file:
> [paste your Agentic UI file link]
> Output as CSS custom properties in tokens.css
> 
> # Implement this component pixel-perfect:
> [paste Figma link]
> React + TypeScript, use CSS variables for all values, include Storybook story.
> 
> # Pull all variables (colors, spacing, type) from this file:
> [paste Figma link]

>    *Updated toast() JS function:*
>    ```javascript
>    const TOAST_MAX=5;
>    const TOAST_DURATION_MS=4000;
>    /* toast(msg) — simple message
>       toast(msg, {type:'success'|'error'|'warn', label:'LABEL TEXT'}) — typed */
>    function toast(msg,opts){
>      let stack=document.getElementById('toastStack');
>      if(!stack){stack=document.createElement('div');stack.id='toastStack';stack.className='toast-stack';document.body.appendChild(stack)}
>      const t=document.createElement('div');
>      const type=(opts&&opts.type)||'';
>      const label=(opts&&opts.label)||(type==='success'?'Success':type==='error'?'Error':type==='warn'?'Warning':'');
>      t.className='toast'+(type?' toast-'+type:'');
>      const ts=new Date();
>      const hh=String(ts.getHours()).padStart(2,'0');
>      const mm=String(ts.getMinutes()).padStart(2,'0');
>      let html='';
>      if(label)html+='<span class="toast-label"></span>';
>      html+='<span class="toast-msg"></span><span class="toast-time">'+hh+':'+mm+'</span>';
>      t.innerHTML=html;
>      if(label)t.querySelector('.toast-label').textContent=label;
>      t.querySelector('.toast-msg').textContent=msg;
>      t.addEventListener('click',()=>dismissToast(t));
>      stack.appendChild(t);
>      requestAnimationFrame(()=>t.classList.add('show'));
>      while(stack.children.length>TOAST_MAX)dismissToast(stack.firstChild);
>      t._timer=setTimeout(()=>dismissToast(t),TOAST_DURATION_MS);
>    }
>    ```

>      **File upload JS handlers** (added before `filterData` function):

>      const _uploadedFiles=[];

>      function renderUploadedFiles(){const list=document.getElementById('uploadFilesList');if(!list)return;list.innerHTML='';_uploadedFiles.forEach((f,i)=>{const chip=document.createElement('div');chip.className='upload-file-chip';chip.innerHTML='<span class="upload-file-chip-name">'+escHtml(f.name)+'</span><span class="upload-file-chip-remove" onclick="removeUploadedFile('+i+')" title="Remove">×</span>';list.appendChild(chip);});}

>      ```

>      **sortTbl() JS function** (added before file upload handlers):
>      ```javascript
>      function sortTbl(th){
>        const tbl=th.closest('table');const tbody=tbl.querySelector('tbody');
>        const rows=Array.from(tbody.querySelectorAll('tr'));
>        const idx=Array.from(th.parentElement.children).indexOf(th);
>        const isDesc=th.classList.contains('sort-desc');
>        tbl.querySelectorAll('th.sortable').forEach(t=>{t.classList.remove('sort-asc','sort-desc')});
>        th.classList.add(isDesc?'sort-asc':'sort-desc');
>        const dir=isDesc?1:-1;
>        rows.sort((a,b)=>{
>          const ac=(a.children[idx]?.textContent||'').trim().toLowerCase();
>          const bc=(b.children[idx]?.textContent||'').trim().toLowerCase();
>          const an=parseFloat(ac.replace(/[^0-9.]/g,''));const bn=parseFloat(bc.replace(/[^0-9.]/g,''));
>          if(!isNaN(an)&&!isNaN(bn))return(an-bn)*dir;
>          return ac<bc?-dir:ac>bc?dir:0;
>        });
>        rows.forEach(r=>tbody.appendChild(r));
>      }
>      ```

> 5. Problem Solving:
>    - **Practical floor at 336 inline styles**: The remaining 336 break into irreducible categories: `display:none` (17, JS-controlled visibility), SVG `color:var(--text-muted)` where `viewBox` sits between `class=` and `style=` attributes (21, can't do simple replace_all), `cursor:pointer` on SVG `<g>` chart elements (12), `cursor:default` (7), `border:none;border-radius:0` form resets (7), SVG dimension attrs `width:9px` (11), and single-prop margin spacings (~40). No clean batch wins remain.
>    - **`.v.text` pattern for JS template strings**: The 14 remaining `style="color:var(--text)"` instances were all on `class="v"` elements inside `.sp-row` (JS template strings). The `.sp-row .v` CSS defaults to `color:var(--text-bright)`, so the inline style was an intentional override. Solution: added `.sp-row .v.text{color:var(--text)}` CSS modifier, then `replace_all` `class="v" style="color:var(--text)"` → `class="v text"`.

> 4. Errors and Fixes:
> 
> - **CSS cascade conflict with `.topnav`**: Early surface-fixes section set `.topnav{background:rgba(250,246,241,0.92)}` but the canonical `.topnav{background:rgba(10,12,16,0.8)}` rule appeared LATER in the CSS and won (last-wins). Fixed by updating the canonical `.topnav` rule directly to cream and adding `.dark .topnav` there, then removing the redundant early override.
> - **CSS cascade conflict with card covers**: Added cream card cover rules in surface-fixes section early in CSS, but original hardcoded-dark card cover rules (`#0f1115`) appeared later and overrode them. Fixed by changing all card cover rules at their original location to use `var(--surface)` instead of hardcoded dark values, making them theme-adaptive.
> - **Redundant surface-fixes entries**: After fixing card covers and topnav at their canonical locations, the early surface-fixes block had redundant rules. Cleaned up by removing the duplicate `.topnav` lines and simplifying the block.
> - **`guides-featured` class missing**: Was referenced in old `.light .guides-featured` rules being converted, but the class doesn't exist in the file. Skipped safely — no effect on output.
> - **`rgba(0,0,0,0.6)` toast shadow override**: Original `.toast` at line ~2823 had heavy dark shadow that would override the warm shadow set earlier. Fixed by updating the canonical `.toast` rule in place.
> 
> 5. Problem Solving:
> 
> - **Light-first CSS architecture**: The previous CSS structure was "inside-out" — dark was in `:root`, cream was in `:root.light`. While display was correct (JS added `.light` class by default), the structure was semantically wrong. Phase 21 fixed this: cream is now truly the default `:root`, dark is `:root.dark`. This makes the CSS coherent and avoids confusion for developers reading the code.
> - **Theme toggle inversion**: Changed `_applyMktTheme` from adding `.light` class (old) to adding `.dark` class (new). The `||'light'` default in `localStorage.getItem('hubify-theme')||'light'` means: no class applied = cream (correct). Dark mode = add `.dark` class.
> - **Card cover theme adaptation**: Instead of maintaining parallel `.light .lab-card-cover.xxx` + `.dark .lab-card-cover.xxx` rules, using `var(--surface)` in the background gradient endpoint makes the cards adapt automatically since `--surface` changes between `:root` (cream `#fdfaf4`) and `:root.dark` (dark `#0f1115`).
> - **Desktop app parity**: The desktop app is a Tauri chrome wrapper that iframes `index.html`. The iframe itself loads the web app (already light mode). The chrome (menu bar, titlebar, dock, notifications) was the only dark-only part — all now converted to Cabinet cream to match the web app.

> 4. Errors and Fixes:
> 
> - **`get_design_context` fails** — Both calls on `123:395` and `178:121` returned "You currently have nothing selected. You need to select a layer first." Fix: fell back to `get_metadata` which works with just fileKey+nodeId and returns structural XML metadata. All subsequent Figma calls use `get_metadata`.

> 
> 5. Problem Solving:
> 
> - **Component extraction strategy** — Since `get_design_context` requires a selection in the Figma desktop app (not available in this context), all component specs are derived from `get_metadata` which provides the structural frame/symbol hierarchy + pixel dimensions. This is sufficient to extract component specs (sizes, states, layout) without visual code output.
> 
> - **Type token formalization** — The TYPOGRAPHY page (`2003:4067`) confirmed all 15 text styles were already correctly recorded in the audit. The value of the Figma call was confirming the `body-text-style-1` node height = 15px (matching body/xs line-height = 15px) and `label-style-*` nodes = 18px height (matching Label/sm line-height = 18px). Added these as CSS custom properties so they can be referenced throughout the file consistently.
> 
> - **Switch thumb math** — Old implementation: 16×16 thumb in 29px-wide track, 0 inset, travel 13px (29-16=13). New: 12×12 thumb, 2px inset each side, travel 15px (29-12-2=15). LG: 20×20 in 43px track, travel 21px (43-20-2=21). This gives standard visual switch padding.
> 
> - **Tooltip dark-on-light pattern** — Initial concern that hardcoded `#191919` tooltip color breaks light mode. Analysis: dark tooltips on light backgrounds is standard industry pattern (Material, shadcn, Radix all do this). The AgenticUI spec explicitly uses `#191919` for tooltip bg. Conclusion: no change needed.

> 2. Key Technical Concepts:
> 
> - **AgenticUI Design System** — fileKey `SjPhSVKTbtE35Xh7PNsmNA`. All 27 components extracted by Phase 26.
> - **Cabinet light mode** — `.light` class on `<html>`, NOT a `dark-mode` class. `:root` is dark by default; `:root.light` is the cream palette.
> - **`toggleTheme()` / `_updateThemeIcons(isLight)`** — existing JS functions that manage `.light` class, `localStorage`, and sidebar icon sync.
> - **`_applySavedTheme()`** — IIFE that reads `localStorage` on page load, defaults to light mode (`saved !== 'dark'`).
> - **`setChatPos(pos)`** — positions chat panel: `'left'` / `'right'` / `'bottom'` / `'hidden'`. Hidden adds `collapsed` to `#chat` + `chat-hidden` to `#workspaceTop`.
> - **`toggleChatVisible()`** — alias that checks `chatPos === 'hidden'` and calls `setChatPos('left'/'hidden')`.
> - **`setChatMode(mode)`** — switches between `'chat'` and `'term'` tabs in the chat pane.
> - **scroll-fade utilities** — `.scroll-fade-y` / `.scroll-fade-x` / `.scroll-fade-bottom` using CSS `mask-image` / `-webkit-mask-image` gradients. Added in Phase 27.
> - **`.switch-with-label`** — AgenticUI compound component from STYLE TESTER-3, 37px row height, label-left + toggle-right. Used in Notifications, Terminal, Appearance settings rows.
> - **`scrollToSettingsSection(navItem, sectionMatch)`** — scrolls settings content to matching `settings-section-label` text, updates active nav item.
> - **`.settings-nav`** — made sticky (`position:sticky; top:16px; max-height:calc(100vh-100px); overflow-y:auto`) in Phase 28 with `scroll-fade-bottom`.
> - **Keyboard shortcuts** — wired in `document.addEventListener('keydown',...)` handler, all using `mod` check (`e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey`).
> - **Dispatch** — not a standalone view; it's `#dispatchFlowCard` inside `#view-overview`. `navTo('dispatch')` is broken.

>   <button ... id="theme-dark-btn" onclick="document.documentElement.classList.remove('light');try{localStorage.setItem('hubify-theme','dark')}catch(e){};_updateThemeIcons(false);toast('Dark theme · macOS-inspired cool blue-gray')">Dark</button>
>   <button ... id="theme-sys-btn" onclick="const sys=window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme:light)').matches;sys?document.documentElement.classList.add('light'):document.documentElement.classList.remove('light');try{localStorage.removeItem('hubify-theme')}catch(e){};_updateThemeIcons(sys);toast('System theme · following OS preference')">System</button>
>   ```
>   
>   `_updateThemeIcons` extended:
>   ```js
>   function _updateThemeIcons(isLight){
>     const moon = document.getElementById('themeIconMoon');
>     const sun = document.getElementById('themeIconSun');
>     const label = document.getElementById('themeLabel');
>     if(moon && sun){
>       moon.style.display = isLight ? '' : 'none';
>       sun.style.display = isLight ? 'none' : '';
>     }
>     if(label) label.textContent = isLight ? 'Light' : 'Dark';
>     // Sync Appearance settings section buttons
>     const lb = document.getElementById('theme-light-btn');
>     const db = document.getElementById('theme-dark-btn');
>     const sb = document.getElementById('theme-sys-btn');

>     if(db) db.className = isLight ? 'btn btn-xs btn-ghost' : 'btn btn-xs btn-primary';
>     if(sb) sb.className = 'btn btn-xs btn-ghost';
>   }
>   ```

> - **Phase 28: Settings nav default active item** — Profile was added as first nav item without `active` class; Models had `active`. Fixed in Phase 29 by swapping: Profile gets `active`, Models loses it. Conventional settings UX: profile/account shown first on open.
> 
> - **Phase 30: Critical — Appearance theme buttons used wrong class**
>   - Was: `document.documentElement.classList.remove('dark-mode')` / `classList.add('dark-mode')`
>   - `dark-mode` class does not exist in CSS. The actual system uses `.light` class on `<html>` for light mode, with `:root` (no class) being dark.
>   - Fix: buttons now call `classList.add/remove('light')` + `localStorage.setItem` + `_updateThemeIcons()`
>   - Also: `_updateThemeIcons()` extended to sync the settings buttons on init (called by `_applySavedTheme()`)
> 
> - **Phase 31: ⌘/ shortcut used wrong element/class**
>   - Was: `const cp=document.getElementById('chatPane');if(cp){const hidden=cp.classList.contains('pos-hidden');setChatPos(hidden?'left':'hidden')}`
>   - `#chatPane` doesn't exist. The chat panel is `#chat`, and hidden state is `chat.classList.contains('collapsed')`. `pos-hidden` is not a real class.
>   - `toggleChatVisible()` already existed and correctly checks `chatPos === 'hidden'`.
>   - Fix: replaced entire broken logic with single `toggleChatVisible()` call.

> - **Settings nav overflow**: 21 sections would clip on short viewports. Fixed by adding `position:sticky; top:16px; max-height:calc(100vh-100px); overflow-y:auto` + `scroll-fade-bottom` class.

> 2. Key Technical Concepts:
>    - **`detailRenderers` object** — canonical sidepeek renderer registry in `v3/index.html`. Each key is a type string; value is `(id) => {tag, title, html}`.
>    - **`openSidepeek(type, id)` / `openDetail(type, id)`** — canonical sidepeek openers. `openSidepeek` is the alias used in HTML onclick attributes.
>    - **`_renderDetail(type, id)`** — falls back to `'No renderer for type: <code>'+type+'</code>'` when no renderer matches — visible broken state when renderer missing.
>    - **Event delegation pattern** — used throughout the `DOMContentLoaded` init block to wire clicks on dynamically-generated or non-onclick HTML elements.
>    - **String concatenation in renderers** — renderers use `'...' + variable + '...'` concatenation to avoid nested backtick issues inside outer template literals.
>    - **`_resolveTaskId(title)` helper** — added in Phase 39; maps card title substrings to T-IDs using a 10-key map.
>    - **`chatAbout(scope, title, context)`** — function at line 11771 that de-dupes chats, creates chat objects, opens the chat panel, and calls toast internally.
>    - **`task` renderer** — keyed by T-xxx IDs (T-101 through T-108); now also T-102 added in Phase 39.
>    - **`comm-event` renderer** — 4-entry registry (xlab-1/2/3/4) for cross-lab comm gateway cards.
>    - **`idea` renderer** — handles `/promote` slash command (`chat-promote-current` key) + future `.idea-row` keys.
>    - **`lab` renderer** — keyed by lab slug: `bigbounce`, `chirality`, `pta-gw`, `quantum-gw`, `sdss-scan`, `erosita-xray`.
>    - **`paper` renderer** — keyed by string numbers: `'1'`, `'2'`, `'3'`, `'4'`.
>    - **`contribution` renderer** — keyed by contribution title strings.

> 2. Key Technical Concepts:
>    - **`chatAbout(scope, title, context)`** — de-dupes chats by scope, creates chat objects, opens panel
>    - **`openSidepeek(type, id)` / `openDetail(type, id)`** — canonical detail opener; openSidepeek is backward-compat alias
>    - **`detailRenderers` object** at line ~12425 — renderer registry: `paper`, `agent`, `experiment`, `contribution`, `figure`, `task`, `comm-event`, `idea`, `standup`, `lab`, `survey`, `wiki`, `alert-rule`, `zone`, `backup-dest`, `cronloop`, etc.
>    - **`AGENT_DEFAULTS`** fallback at line 12816 — unknown agent IDs fall back via `Object.assign({}, AGENT_DEFAULTS, agents[id] || agents['bigbounce-orchestrator'])`
>    - **DOMContentLoaded delegation pattern** — all new wiring inserted before Phase 46 comment (now line ~17200); uses `if(el.onclick)return;` guard
>    - **`navTo(viewId)`** — navigates to named view; all view IDs are `view-{name}` prefixed
>    - **`_resolveTaskId(title)`** — maps descriptive strings → T-xxx task IDs (10-key map)
>    - **`_resolveContribKey(text)`** — substring mapper for contribution renderer keys
>    - **`e.stopPropagation()`** — used in nested elements to prevent parent handler interference
>    - **`if(item.closest('#view-alerts, #view-standups'))return;`** — exclusion pattern to avoid double-wiring already-handled views

> 2. Key Technical Concepts:
>    - **`chatAbout(scope, title, context)`** — de-dupes chats by scope, creates chat objects, opens panel. Used for all "discovery/navigation" type actions
>    - **`openSidepeek(type, id)` / `openDetail(type, id)`** — canonical detail opener for entities (agent, lab, paper, experiment, file, etc.)
>    - **`openFile(filename)`** — opens rich file preview in tab (defined at line 18385)
>    - **`navTo(viewId)`** — navigates to named view (e.g., `navTo('settings')`)
>    - **`window.open(url, '_blank')`** — for opening real URLs
>    - **`toast('...')`** — only for intentional action confirmations (deploy, restart, copy, download, etc.). Should NOT be used for navigation/discovery
>    - **DOMContentLoaded delegation pattern** — for wiring elements that share CSS classes
>    - **`Date.now()%10000`** — used for unique chat scope IDs when no stable identifier exists
>    - **Phase 41 `.skill-row` override** — DOMContentLoaded delegation that nulls inline `toast()` onclick on all `.skill-row` elements and replaces with `openSkillDetail()`. ~196 skill-row toasts are intercepted at runtime; their HTML still contains `toast()` but it's never executed
>    - **Template literal context** — when editing JS template literals (backtick strings), `${variable}` expressions are evaluated at render time; `toast(\'...\')` within JS string concatenation uses escaped quotes
>    - **String concatenation in renderers** — agent/project/figure sidepeek renderers use `'...' + variable + '...'` concatenation for dynamic content

> 2. Key Technical Concepts:
>    - **`chatAbout(scope, title, context)`** — de-dupes chats by scope, creates chat objects, opens panel. Used for all "discovery/navigation/workflow" type actions
>    - **`openSidepeek(type, id)` / `openDetail(type, id)`** — canonical detail opener for entities
>    - **`openFile(filename)`** — opens rich file preview in tab
>    - **`navTo(viewId)`** — navigates to named view
>    - **`window.open(url, '_blank')`** — for opening real external URLs
>    - **`toast('...')`** — ONLY for intentional action confirmations (deploy, restart, download, copy, delete, save, etc.). Should NOT be used for navigation/discovery/workflow
>    - **Phase 41 `.skill-row` override** — DOMContentLoaded delegation nulls inline `toast()` onclick on all `.skill-row` elements and replaces with `openSkillDetail()`. ~196 skill-row toasts are intercepted at runtime; their HTML still contains `toast()` but it's never executed
>    - **Template literal context** — `${variable}` expressions work inside backtick strings; nested template literals valid: `` ${cond ? `...${id}...` : `...${id}...`} ``
>    - **String concatenation in renderers** — agent/project/figure sidepeek renderers use `'...' + variable + '...'` concatenation with `\'` for inner escaped quotes
>    - **Non-intentional vs intentional toast distinction**: Intentional = action confirmations (download, compile, restart, delete, save, promote). Non-intentional = discovery/navigation/workflow triggers that should open context

>    - Typography: Departure Mono for labels (`--label-mono`), Geist for body (`--geist`), JetBrains Mono for code (`--mono`)
>    - Segmented control pattern: pill tray bg (`surface-2`), `r-pill` radius, active = raised chip with `elev-1` shadow
>    - Collapsible nav sections: chevron toggle, `display:none` by default, `toggleNavSection()` JS
>    - Sage discipline: no neon glow on status dots (`box-shadow:none!important`), accent only for small status indicators, never on buttons/CTAs/hero
>    - Border consistency: `--border-strong` (1px) for all content cards/inputs, `--border-bright` on hover, 0.5px reserved for floating overlays
>    - Project context switcher: `selectProject()` updates sidebar counts, project button, and Director view subline
>    - Responsive sidebar: 3 breakpoints (1280px full, 1024px icon rail, 768px mobile slide-out overlay)

>      **Collapsible nav CSS added:**
>      ```css
>      .sb-collapsible-hdr{cursor:pointer;user-select:none}
>      .sb-collapsible-hdr .sb-nav-chevron{
>        width:12px;height:12px;flex-shrink:0;color:var(--text-dim);
>        transition:transform .15s ease;
>      }
>      .sb-collapsible-hdr.open .sb-nav-chevron{transform:rotate(90deg)}
>      .nav-collapse-body{overflow:hidden}
>      .nav-collapse-foot{
>        display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;

>        font-family:var(--label-mono);font-size:10px;font-weight:600;

>        color:var(--text-dim);cursor:pointer;
>        border-radius:var(--r-md);transition:color .1s;
>      }
>      .nav-collapse-foot:hover{color:var(--text);background:var(--surface-2)}
>      ```
> 
>      **Nav section separators:**
>      ```css
>      .nav-section{padding:0 0 4px}
>      .nav-section+.nav-section{border-top:1px solid var(--border);padding-top:4px;margin-top:2px}
>      ```
> 
>      **Collapsible nav JS:**
>      ```javascript
>      function toggleNavSection(hdr){
>        hdr.classList.toggle('open');
>        const body=hdr.nextElementSibling;
>        if(!body||!body.classList.contains('nav-collapse-body'))return;
>        if(hdr.classList.contains('open')){body.style.display='block'}
>        else{body.style.display='none'}
>      }
>      ```
